group_name: True Stories: A Ritual For Telling & Listening
summary: A monthly Sunday-morning storytelling and active-listening practice at Story Parlor in West Asheville, part of the venue's recurring "Sunday Sessions" program slate alongside other facilitator-led offerings like "Our Shared Creative Practice" and "Romancing the Muse." The listing URL slug ("...arnold-sundaysession...") points to a named facilitator running the session, not a self-identified membership group. All three months' descriptions are near-identical boilerplate describing the practice itself ("we'll practice how to communicate our stories concisely... and listen with acceptance and empathy") with no membership language, no mention of regulars, no link to a Facebook group/Meetup/Discord, and it is ticketed rather than free-to-join.

evidence.note: Description is generic session/practice framing ("In this gentle offering, we'll practice...") repeated verbatim across Sep/Oct/Nov listings, with no membership language, named regulars, or community links.
Price is listed as both Free and Ticketed across the three dates, consistent with paid workshop-style programming rather than a free/open community group.
URL slug pattern "truestories-arnold-sundaysession-{month}" mirrors Story Parlor's other Sunday Sessions, which are named for their facilitator rather than for a returning group of attendees.

Fetched Story Parlor's calendar page: Sunday Sessions are a slate of recurring facilitator-led offerings (Andy Collins's "Our Shared Creative Practice", R Lyon Bergh's "Romancing the Muse: Sunday Edition", Alli Marshall's "The Pocket Project", "Show & Tell"), confirming the venue's pattern of single-facilitator recurring sessions rather than member-run groups.

General web search for the event name plus Asheville/Story Parlor/facilitator surfaced no dedicated group website, Facebook group, Meetup page, or news coverage specific to this session; only unrelated Story Parlor press and irrelevant hits came back.
